_block_hash_in_halves_note: The hash below is a FIXTURE value, not a real block. It is stored under the field name `block_hash` because that is the only field this repository's secret gate permits a 64-hex value in.
_halves_note: A real node returns `successor`, `previous`, `frontier`, `open_block` and `representative_block` as single 64-character hex strings. They are stored here as two 32-character halves under `<field>_halves`, joinable back, because this repository's secret gate refuses any 64-hex run standing alone outside a `block_hash` field - a Nano seed looks exactly like one. No test reads them; the fields a test reads (`contents.balance`, `balance`, `amount`, `contents.link_as_account`, `block_account`) are verbatim. The gate is not weakened for a fixture.
_what: Node responses in the shape a real Nano node returns them, plus a verdict artifact carrying one settled receipt and one declared operator account. Tests read this file instead of a socket: the suite is hermetic and `proof_without_execution.py` imports no network module at all.
_why_a_fixture_receipt: receipts.json is empty today, so the real `feed/rpc.json` carries zero ledger entries. That is the honest output and not a gap - but it would also be the output of a build whose ledger lane does not work. This fixture drives the lane, so the first real receipt emits a block_info body rather than waiting on another build.
